articulation.label: person
articulation.alt: person: /p/ → /ɝ/ → /s/ → /ə/ → /n/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /p/: Close the lips, then release the air.
/ɝ/: Bunch the tongue for American r; no tip contact.
/s/: Make a narrow gap near the ridge; let air flow.
/ə/: Relax the tongue in the center.
/n/: Tip at the ridge; air goes through the nose.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

cards.title: Your A1 checkpoint
sections: Try the five tasks before opening the models. A partner may speak slowly or repeat. Listen to the dictation and write what you hear.
Meet someone. Give and spell a real or invented name, then ask their name.
Ask where someone is from and say where you are from.
Say these numbers, then write them from memory: 11, 14, 16, 19, 20.
Fill in a short form: first name, last name and an invented phone number.

Ask for help when you miss a word.
Review words: correct, age, Friday, plus, wrong. Cover the list; recall meanings and use two in your own sentences.
cards.name: Everyday English - A1 - Day 030 - Review & Check - 01

cards.answer:
Dictation: A new person joins the class.
1: For example: Hello. I’m Mei. M-E-I. What’s your name?
2: For example: Where are you from? I’m from Japan.
3: eleven; fourteen; sixteen; nineteen; twenty
4: Check that the letters and digits match the information you give aloud.
5: For example: Please say it again. Please speak slowly.
For each task, note: I can do it; I can do it with repetition; I need more practice. Repeat difficult tasks another day with new details. Clear meaning matters more than a perfect accent.
